learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected one possible message for random once-used four-bit key and sent1101,then locked it in.
observations.exploration: Flipped bit1: message1000,key0101. Bit2:1100,key0001. Bit4:1101,key0000. Counter rose1,2,3; Fill in rest unlocked. Pressed it: sixteen distinct message/key pairs,16 of16; bit controls disabled,reveal unlocked.
observations.reveal: Cites three hand-picked messages and all sixteen different keys. Sent1101 rules nothing out with random key; trying keys only lists messages. One-time-pad condition key never reused.
observations.visual: Inline screenshot inspected: message,key,sent rows align four bits; sixteen green outlined message-key tiles and16 of16 count readable. Trust5/5 ignored.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884122 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: Clear exhaustive-key question tests unique-decryption intuition with random once-used condition.

interaction.reason: Bit changes generate distinct keys while ciphertext fixed,then exhaustive mapping confirms.

payoff.reason: Uses exact hand-picked messages to explain no elimination and key-reuse limit.
payoff.evidence: Reveal names three choices and never-reuse condition.

clarity.reason: Aligned rows,brief XOR definition and grid make tested path understandable.

visualExplanation.evidence: Final screenshot and three hand cases.

playfulness.evidence: Three flips including zero-key identity case.

depth.reason: XOR mapping,exhaustive possibilities and key-use condition linked.

complexity.reason: Coordinates message,key,ciphertext and inference over all possible keys.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: four bit toggles and fill button.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: moderate: binary strings and aligned bit operation

whyCool: Choosing the intercepted bits themselves as the message produces an all-zero key,yet every other message still gets its own compatible key.
caveat: Fixed ciphertext and four-bit example; key reuse and nonuniform-message assumptions not explored.
